knowledgeGraph.policy: Candidate discovery only; every conclusion below was rechecked against the pinned Castle worktree.

currentBatch.name: Ordinary AOGM exploration and services certification
currentBatch.selectionRationale: Move from the completed combat route to ordinary application depth: Camp/Rest and money operations are ready for certification, while contextual service entry supplies their normal exploration handoff. Missing combat subcommands and broad item/spell edge cases remain separate implementation batches.

scopes.name: Classic Realmz application
scopes.definition: Every distinct player-visible task or interaction sequence exposed by the pinned Castle application.

scopes.name: Modern Realmz 2.0 host
scopes.definition: Required package, vault, settings, failure, and release workflows that are not part of the Classic denominator.

exclusions.name: Legacy registration, order-form, contact, and accessory launching
exclusions.reason: Player-visible in the historical executable but not gameplay and not meaningful in a freely distributed modern host; retained as an evidenced exclusion rather than counted as application completeness.

exclusions.name: Developer and cheat controls
exclusions.reason: Developer-only state changes are explicitly outside the player-visible workflow denominator.

exclusions.name: Internal helpers, formulas, and file decoding
exclusions.reason: These support workflows but are not distinct player interactions; their behavior belongs in differential cases and rule tests.

exclusions.name: General player item storage
exclusions.reason: Castle exposes trade, dropping, shops, and scenario equipment escrow but no ordinary player-operated item stash. The generic 2.0 storage intent is intentionally rejected unless new source evidence appears.

workflows.name: Select a scenario
workflows.trigger: Choose New Game or open the campaign library.
workflows.interactionSequence: Browse installed scenarios, inspect the selected title, and confirm selection.
workflows.committedOutcome: The selected immutable campaign becomes the setup context without beginning play.

gaps.summary: Only AOGM has ordinary campaign-selection evidence in 2.0.
gaps.evidence: Package tests are synthetic and the ordinary route evidence is AOGM-specific.
gaps.nextAction: Select and enter War through the ordinary campaign library.

workflows.name: View campaign restrictions
workflows.trigger: Select a scenario before party assembly.
workflows.interactionSequence: Read party-size, level, race, caste, and authored restriction guidance.
workflows.committedOutcome: No state changes; party eligibility is understandable before selection.

workflows.name: Assemble the active party
workflows.trigger: A campaign has been selected.
workflows.interactionSequence: Add eligible characters, import reusable characters, remove selections, and review the editable roster.
workflows.committedOutcome: The setup roster remains editable until Begin Adventure commits it to session state.

workflows.name: Create a character
workflows.trigger: Choose Create Character from party setup or the Character menu.
workflows.interactionSequence: Enter identity, choose race then eligible class, choose appearance, generate and review the deterministic draft, select spells when eligible, and finalize.
workflows.committedOutcome: A complete levelled character joins setup and may be published as a reusable revision.

gaps.summary: The five-step creator has deterministic and UI tests but no recorded ordinary AOGM completion in the audit evidence.
gaps.evidence: Current labels stop at route-harness coverage.
gaps.nextAction: Create and add one character through the ordinary AOGM setup UI.

workflows.name: Inspect a reusable character before play
workflows.trigger: Select a character during party setup.
workflows.interactionSequence: Open the complete sheet, equipment, conditions, spells, portrait, and tactical icon before deciding eligibility or inclusion.
workflows.committedOutcome: No gameplay state changes; the player can make an informed party choice.

workflows.name: Alter the party
workflows.trigger: Choose Alter Party before play or use the supported setup roster controls.
workflows.interactionSequence: Remove or replace party members while eligibility and maximum-party rules remain enforced.
workflows.committedOutcome: The editable setup roster changes; active-play mutations do not silently publish to reusable characters.

workflows.name: Begin the adventure
workflows.trigger: Confirm an eligible non-empty setup party.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate the final roster and choose Begin Adventure.
workflows.committedOutcome: Party setup commits once, play begins at the campaign start, and the boundary is saveable.

workflows.name: End the active adventure
workflows.trigger: Choose End Game while a campaign is active.
workflows.interactionSequence: Confirm leaving the current campaign and return to scenario selection without conflating quit or save.
workflows.committedOutcome: The active session closes at a committed boundary and the campaign library returns.

gaps.summary: End Adventure has synthetic interaction and teardown proof but no ordinary AOGM acceptance.
gaps.evidence: The workflow has not yet been exercised from active AOGM play.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise save-and-end, cancel, and discard-and-end from active AOGM play after the lifecycle-hook compiler gap closes.

gaps.summary: Save-before-close ordering is characterized through the host transaction and repositories separately, but has no full composition-root failure-injection test.
gaps.evidence: Focused tests prove save failure suppresses close and SaveRepository validates writes transactionally; they do not yet inject each repository failure through RealmzApplication.
gaps.nextAction: Add a bounded root-level repository double that proves pre-close snapshot identity, failure retention, no-write discard, and successful campaign return without scanning installed packages.

workflows.name: Travel on land and in dungeons
workflows.trigger: Use keyboard, keypad, or mouse direction input in exploration.
workflows.interactionSequence: Probe the authoritative topology, move in eight land directions or four dungeon directions, cross transitions, advance time, fire the selected AP, then check random encounters.
workflows.committedOutcome: Location, overlays, time, trigger continuation, and RNG advance deterministically.

gaps.summary: Dungeon and boat variants lack ordinary campaign certification.
gaps.evidence: AOGM land movement is observed; other variants are synthetic or route-harness only.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise one dungeon transition and one boat/shore route in ordinary play.

gaps.summary: Ordinary positive-tile blocked land movement now advances the attempted tile time and runs current-cell random checks, while zero/negative tiles, boat/shore cancellation, special dungeon walls, and timed-location deltas remain unresolved.
gaps.evidence: buttonchoice.c charges mapstats time on ordinary blocked land terrain but uses three clicks for zero/negative tiles and suppresses timing on some boat/shore paths; threed.c times special wall paths but not an ordinary solid wall. The bounded GameSession path now retains a blocked target cell and drains a post-time continuation without moving.
gaps.nextAction: Use controlled fixtures for zero/negative land tiles, boat/shore cancellation, special dungeon wall bits, and attempted-coordinate timed gates before broadening the topology result.

workflows.name: Search the current location
workflows.trigger: Choose Search while exploring.
workflows.interactionSequence: Perform the source-ordered secret and trigger search, advance the applicable time, and present discoveries.
workflows.committedOutcome: Discovery overlays and time are committed once and can be restored.

workflows.name: Camp and rest
workflows.trigger: Toggle Camp or choose Rest in a legal exploration state.
workflows.interactionSequence: Enter camp mode, expose camp-only commands, choose rest duration, process time, fatigue, healing, conditions, and interruptions, then leave camp.
workflows.committedOutcome: Clock and party recovery state advance through one serializable operation.

workflows.name: Observe time, fatigue, and light
workflows.trigger: Travel, search, camp, rest, or execute an action that advances time.
workflows.interactionSequence: Advance the Realmz clock, decay conditions and light, accumulate fatigue, cross midnight, and stage any age or timed-event interaction.
workflows.committedOutcome: All time-derived state and pending interactions remain deterministic and saveable.

workflows.name: Cast a numeric fast spell
workflows.trigger: Press a configured numeric spell shortcut during exploration.
workflows.interactionSequence: Resolve the configured caster/spell, validate the current context, choose any required target, cast, and return to exploration.
workflows.committedOutcome: The same spell operation and costs apply as the ordinary field spell path.

gaps.summary: Numeric fast-spell configuration and invocation are absent and their save ownership is not yet traced end to end.
gaps.evidence: Castle dispatches numeric keys, while 2.0 has no shortcut configuration model.
gaps.nextAction: Trace the preference/save fields and ordinary cast handoff, then decide whether the shortcut is Classic state or presentation state.

workflows.name: Enter a contextual service
workflows.trigger: A scenario enables a shop or temple and the player chooses its exploration command.
workflows.interactionSequence: Expose only the enabled service, enter its typed workspace, complete or cancel operations, then return to exploration.
workflows.committedOutcome: Service availability and any completed transactions remain session-owned and saveable.

gaps.summary: Contextual service entry is not yet demonstrated through ordinary AOGM play.
gaps.evidence: Current evidence is synthetic or route-harness only.
gaps.nextAction: Reach and enter one AOGM contextual service through ordinary exploration.

workflows.name: Trigger a placed Action Point
workflows.trigger: Movement, search, start-on, return, or relocation reaches an authored AP condition.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select the first native AP record, apply chance and lifecycle rules, execute its scenario program, preserve origin through XAP/GOSUB, and perform the one destination recheck.
workflows.committedOutcome: World mutations, VM continuation, pending interaction, and RNG are committed in source order.

workflows.name: Present staged text, picture, and sound
workflows.trigger: A scenario action displays text, a picture, scrolling text, or sound.
workflows.interactionSequence: Render the active Classic textbox/picture stage, play sound with source-backed channel behavior, wait when acknowledgement is required, then move completed narrative to history.
workflows.committedOutcome: Only completed narrative enters history; the pending stage and VM continuation survive save and restore.

gaps.summary: Only AOGM's opening media sequence has ordinary-play evidence.
gaps.evidence: The remaining media variants are covered by synthetic and route tests.
gaps.nextAction: Capture an ordinary second-campaign message/picture/sound sequence.

workflows.name: Choose a scenario response
workflows.trigger: A Yes/No, Data OD, Simple Encounter, or indexed choice requires input.
workflows.interactionSequence: Display source-backed labels, accept exactly one response, validate its request ID and shape, and resume the issuing VM frame.
workflows.committedOutcome: The selected branch executes once and the response boundary remains saveable.

workflows.name: Resolve a complex or thief encounter
workflows.trigger: A scenario enters Complex, Thief, or word/action encounter flow.
workflows.interactionSequence: Present the available action vocabulary, collect any word or thief choice, execute the selected result, and resume the originating scenario frame.
workflows.committedOutcome: Encounter state, selected action, VM frame, and resulting mutations are serialized together.

gaps.summary: Thief encounter action availability and result routing are not fully traced or represented.
gaps.evidence: The typed complex interaction exists, but the Castle thief branch has no complete workflow fixture.
gaps.nextAction: Build a synthetic thief encounter oracle fixture and reconcile Providence fields and typed responses.

workflows.name: Select a character, ally, item, spell, or ability subject
workflows.trigger: A scenario action requests a typed subject picker.
workflows.interactionSequence: Filter legal candidates, show source-relevant details, select one stable domain ID, or reject cancellation when mandatory.
workflows.committedOutcome: The issuing scenario frame receives one validated selection and resumes exactly once.

gaps.summary: Picker variants are tested synthetically but not all observed in ordinary AOGM play.
gaps.evidence: No ordinary-play label covers item, spell, ally, and ability selections together.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise reachable AOGM picker variants and retain exact unsupported variants in the parity queue.

workflows.name: Enter a random or timed encounter
workflows.trigger: Movement/time satisfies a random rectangle or timed encounter check.
workflows.interactionSequence: Evaluate the source-ordered gate with session RNG and clock, select the authored encounter, stage interactions, and return to exploration or the resulting workspace.
workflows.committedOutcome: Clock, RNG draw order, encounter continuation, and any transition remain deterministic and saveable.

gaps.summary: Timed records dispatch through a save-owned scheduler, but location-changing and post-action-destination timed programs lack a dedicated end-to-end fixture.
gaps.evidence: The scheduler rebases its remaining scan and later random regions after an active timed VM program, while current tests prove staged text, eligibility, mutation, recovery, and save/resume without a timed-program relocation.
gaps.nextAction: Add a synthetic timed AP that changes map or coordinate, yields, applies any source-owned AP destination semantics, resumes the remaining scan, and performs the final random check at the resulting location.

workflows.name: View a character sheet
workflows.trigger: Choose Characters or select a party member for details.
workflows.interactionSequence: Inspect identity, attributes, combat statistics, personal wealth, conditions, saves, equipment, spells, special modifiers and abilities, race and caste definitions, all five aging bands, and the lifetime record without mutating state.
workflows.committedOutcome: No gameplay state changes; displayed legality and values come from the detached view.

gaps.summary: Castle's lifetime combat record and prestige cannot yet be calculated accurately.
gaps.evidence: CharacterState retains only prestige penalty; it does not own Castle's lifetime hits, misses, damage, kills, deaths, knockouts, turns, spells, and destroyed-foe counters.
gaps.nextAction: Add source-backed lifetime counters and update every owning combat and magic mutation path before enabling the visible Lifetime Record tab.

gaps.summary: Several nonzero Classic ability slots lack verified display names.
gaps.evidence: The pinned Castle source indexes native STR# labels that are not present in the source tree; Realmz 2.0 preserves those exact slots and values with explicit generic labels.
gaps.nextAction: Recover the stock STR# labels from an authoritative legal resource fixture before replacing generic slot names.

workflows.name: Change portrait or combat icon
workflows.trigger: Choose the Character menu portrait or icon command.
workflows.interactionSequence: Browse the package-backed catalog, preview one identity, confirm or cancel, and return to character view.
workflows.committedOutcome: The selected portrait or tactical icon stable ID changes and persists.

workflows.name: Reorder the party
workflows.trigger: Choose Party Order from the Character menu.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select a party member and move that member to the desired slot while preserving identity and state.
workflows.committedOutcome: Party slot order changes and drives later selection and battle formation order.

workflows.name: Acknowledge a live age-band update
workflows.trigger: Clock or spell processing crosses a character age-band boundary.
workflows.interactionSequence: Pause the exact continuation, show the new band/range and fifteen deltas in target order, request sound, acknowledge, and resume.
workflows.committedOutcome: The age mutation and continuation are committed once and remain saveable while pending.

gaps.summary: Age updates have no ordinary-campaign observation because the trigger is rare.
gaps.evidence: Only deterministic fixtures and continuation tests exercise the workflow.
gaps.nextAction: Retain it in the parity queue until an ordinary route reaches it.

workflows.name: Inspect allies and the bestiary
workflows.trigger: Choose Allies or Bestiary from the menu.
workflows.interactionSequence: Browse known entries, inspect visible statistics and media, and return without mutation.
workflows.committedOutcome: No gameplay state changes; only source-permitted knowledge is displayed.

gaps.summary: The allies and bestiary workspaces are absent and the known-entry display contract is incomplete.
gaps.evidence: No route or presenter renders Castle's beast workflow.
gaps.nextAction: Trace discovery visibility, complete the immutable display model, and build read-only workspaces.

workflows.name: Equip and unequip carried items
workflows.trigger: Open Inventory for a party member outside combat or an encounter.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select an item, inspect legal slots and restrictions, equip or unequip it, and refresh derived combat values.
workflows.committedOutcome: The exact item instance and equipment state change once and remain saveable.

gaps.summary: The declared split/join intents are dead and may not represent a real Classic player workflow.
gaps.evidence: Castle compacts item records internally, but no distinct player split/join control has been established.
gaps.nextAction: Trace every items.c branch before deleting the intents or implementing a stack operation.

workflows.name: Inspect an item
workflows.trigger: Select Show Item or an inventory detail action.
workflows.interactionSequence: Display identification, description, category, restrictions, charges, value, curse/equipment state, and legal actions.
workflows.committedOutcome: No gameplay state changes; unknown fields stay hidden according to identification state.

workflows.name: Use an item
workflows.trigger: Choose Use for a carried item in field, camp, or combat context.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate context and charges, collect any target, execute the source-backed effect, decrement charges, and present results.
workflows.committedOutcome: Effect, target state, charges, continuation, and RNG commit atomically.

gaps.summary: Fixed-power charged items and field scroll scribing/use now preserve exact targets, charges/load, five-slot state, sound, save/resume, and transactional cancellation; combat scrolls, discard, case transfer, door/XAP items, random-power combat, spatial/repeated targets, and broader specials remain explicit.
gaps.evidence: Castle's common item path plus makescroll/getscroll establish the implemented field branches. Separate combat, discard, case-transfer, door, missile-class, target-shape, and abort branches remain bounded gaps.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise an ordinary AOGM charged item and scroll route, then characterize combat scroll, discard, case-transfer, door/XAP, random-power combat, and target-abort behavior separately.

workflows.name: Trade an item between characters
workflows.trigger: Choose Trade and select source item and recipient.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate capacity and equipment state, choose a recipient, transfer the exact instance as unequipped, or reject.
workflows.committedOutcome: Ownership changes once while identity, charges, curse, and identification remain intact.

gaps.summary: Trade has no ordinary campaign observation.
gaps.evidence: Only integration and presentation tests cover it.
gaps.nextAction: Trade one charged item in AOGM and verify save/reload.

workflows.name: Drop an item
workflows.trigger: Choose Drop for a removable carried item.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate removal, present irreversible confirmation, cancel or remove the exact instance, and return.
workflows.committedOutcome: Confirmed removal commits once; cancellation leaves state unchanged.

workflows.name: Identify an item
workflows.trigger: Choose a shop identification service or another source-backed identification action.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select an unidentified item, pay or resolve the effect, reveal identity, and refresh actions and value.
workflows.committedOutcome: Identification state and payment commit atomically and persist.

gaps.summary: Shop identification works, but IDENTIFY_ITEM is dead and non-shop identification is unclassified.
gaps.evidence: Service identification is implemented; no GameSession dispatch exists for IDENTIFY_ITEM.
gaps.nextAction: Trace spell, item, and scenario identification paths and assign or remove the generic intent.

workflows.name: Temporarily escrow and restore equipment
workflows.trigger: A scenario action removes or restores party equipment.
workflows.interactionSequence: Move exact instances to session escrow, preserve them, and restore according to authored sequence.
workflows.committedOutcome: Party and escrow inventories remain saveable through VM continuation.

workflows.name: Choose a spell, power, and target
workflows.trigger: Open the spellbook in field, camp, or combat context.
workflows.interactionSequence: Filter castable spells, show costs and failure reasons, choose legal power, then select character, actor, repeated actors, or battlefield area.
workflows.committedOutcome: One complete CAST_SPELL intent owns the selection; abandoned presentation choices do not mutate simulation.

gaps.summary: SELECT_SPELL_POWER and SELECT_SPELL_TARGET are dead scaffolding beside the complete CAST_SPELL payload.
gaps.evidence: GameSession dispatches CAST_SPELL and not the incremental kinds.
gaps.nextAction: Remove or explicitly reserve the dead kinds after confirming no presenter depends on them.

workflows.name: Cast field and camp spells
workflows.trigger: Choose Spells during exploration or camp, including Get or Make Scroll.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate context, choose power and target, pay cost, resolve effect and interaction, or create/use a scroll where permitted.
workflows.committedOutcome: Spell points, item state, targets, clock effects, continuations, and RNG commit atomically.

gaps.summary: Field casting, camp mode, five-slot scroll persistence, parchment-backed Make Scroll, and transactional no-SP field scroll use are implemented; combat scroll use, invalid-field discard, case transfer, allied targets, and map effects remain explicit.
gaps.evidence: The source-backed field and scribing paths are deterministic and saveable. Castle's combat branch, discard prompt, type-13 trade coupling, allied held-over targets, and map mutations still require complete typed ownership.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise the field scroll workflow in ordinary AOGM play, then implement combat/discard/case-transfer branches only from their bounded differential evidence.

workflows.name: Cast a spell in combat
workflows.trigger: The active character or a monster chooses a legal magical attack.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select spell, power, and target; validate range and LOS; spend costs/actions; resolve defenses, effects, deaths, and macros; advance actor.
workflows.committedOutcome: Battle state, resources, action budget, macro queues, RNG, and interactions remain serializable.

workflows.name: Swap money between characters
workflows.trigger: Choose Swap from exploration.
workflows.interactionSequence: Choose source and destination characters, denomination and amount, validate wealth, then transfer or cancel.
workflows.committedOutcome: Character wealth changes without creating or losing money and persists.

workflows.name: Pool and share party money
workflows.trigger: Choose Pool or Share.
workflows.interactionSequence: Collect eligible character wealth into the pool or redistribute pooled denominations according to Classic rules.
workflows.committedOutcome: Total party wealth is conserved and the new distribution persists.

workflows.name: Use a shop
workflows.trigger: Opcode 6 opens a shop or the contextual Shop command is chosen.
workflows.interactionSequence: Browse stock, buy, sell, identify for twenty gold, use buyback stock, and leave.
workflows.committedOutcome: Stock, item ownership, identification, and wealth commit atomically and persist.

gaps.summary: Normalized shop stock omits native empty-slot provenance.
gaps.evidence: Providence emits occupied stock in order but cannot reproduce Castle's first-empty buyback slot exactly.
gaps.nextAction: Preserve native stock slot identity if certified content proves player-visible ordering depends on it.

gaps.summary: The complete shop lifecycle has no ordinary campaign certification.
gaps.evidence: Source-backed and persistence tests exist, but no AOGM ordinary-play label.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise buy, sell, identify, buyback, leave, and reload in an ordinary shop.

workflows.name: Use a temple
workflows.trigger: Opcode 32 enables a temple and the contextual command is chosen.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select one of nine services and a character, calculate signed percentage cost, pay pooled then personal gold, apply mutation, and leave.
workflows.committedOutcome: Wealth, character state, temple definition, and pending response persist together.

gaps.summary: The implemented temple subset has no ordinary campaign certification.
gaps.evidence: Tests cover the fixed services, but ordinary AOGM entry and reload are unrecorded.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise representative temple mutations and no-op payment in ordinary play.

workflows.name: Use the bank
workflows.trigger: Opcode 49 enables bank-backed Swap and the player chooses the contextual bank command.
workflows.interactionSequence: Move every deposited denomination into the shared pool once, then use Pool, Share, exact character transfers, and Done before location departure returns the remaining pool to the bank.
workflows.committedOutcome: Gold, gems, and jewelry retain exact ownership across bank entry, Swap, save/restore, Done, and departure cleanup.

gaps.summary: The complete bank-backed Swap lifecycle has no ordinary campaign certification.
gaps.evidence: Source-backed simulation, save/restore, movement cleanup, and presentation tests are synthetic or route-harness evidence.
gaps.nextAction: Exercise bank entry, denomination transfer, Done, departure cleanup, and reload in an ordinary campaign with a reachable bank.

workflows.name: Enter and set up a battle
workflows.trigger: A scenario battle opcode or random encounter starts combat.
workflows.interactionSequence: Resolve surprise and battle definition, build the tactical field, place party/allies/monsters, establish conditions and initiative, and stage the first actor.
workflows.committedOutcome: The complete battlefield, footprints, actors, initiative, RNG, and originating VM continuation are saveable before the first action.

workflows.name: Control an active combat turn
workflows.trigger: Initiative selects a living party, ally, or monster actor.
workflows.interactionSequence: Expose legal actions and reasons, retain actor/action/target state through continuations, resolve automatic actors, and advance only after the action budget or turn ends.
workflows.committedOutcome: Actor, attacks, movement, selected action, target, and next source row remain deterministic and serializable.

gaps.summary: The Classic turn workspace still lacks Auto Character Move, the independently saved per-character Auto toggle, Delay, Undo, Bandage, and conditional Turn Undead.
gaps.evidence: Castle combat and combatchoice expose these as distinct stateful commands. The reconstructed full-width deck now keeps implemented Guard, Finish, Weapon, Attack, Spells, Items, and Escape available without inventing responses for commands whose simulation or persistence contract is absent.
gaps.nextAction: Characterize Delay, Undo, Bandage, both Auto concepts, and Turn Undead as separate source-backed workflows, including save ownership, then add typed actions one coherent subset at a time.

workflows.name: Move on the tactical battlefield
workflows.trigger: The active actor chooses movement or monster AI advances toward/away from a target.
workflows.interactionSequence: Probe an eight-direction destination with complete-footprint terrain cost, LOS/adjacency and reaction rules, commit one step, and repeat while movement remains.
workflows.committedOutcome: Position, movement budget, reaction continuations, targets, and RNG remain saveable.

gaps.summary: Realmz 2.0 requires an explicit switch from missile to melee before hostile collision, while Castle can perform that switch through its Auto Weapon Switch preference.
gaps.evidence: The pinned collision branch proves that Target is the charged item/missile picker and that movement into an opposed footprint owns melee. For ordinary physical missiles it either warns or jumps through gomelee according to autoweapswitch; 2.0 currently exposes one explicit deterministic switch command instead of this optional convenience behavior.
gaps.nextAction: Decide whether Auto Weapon Switch belongs in modern host settings or whether explicit switching is the single 2.0 workflow, then record the decision and cover missile-mode collision accordingly.

workflows.name: Make melee and missile attacks
workflows.trigger: An active actor chooses a legal physical target or monster AI resolves an authored attack row.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate weapon/mode/range/LOS, consume source-ordered rolls, resolve hit, damage, specials, defenses, fumbles, reactions and deaths, then spend action budget.
workflows.committedOutcome: Health, conditions, equipment, charges, dropped-item queue, RNG, macro queue, and actor cadence persist together.

workflows.name: Switch melee and missile weapon mode
workflows.trigger: The active party character chooses the weapon-mode control.
workflows.interactionSequence: Select an equipped legal melee or missile weapon, switch mode without spending attacks/movement/turn, and refresh legal targets.
workflows.committedOutcome: Per-character battle weapon mode and selected item persist without falling through to another resolver.

workflows.name: Guard or finish a turn
workflows.trigger: The active player character chooses Guard or Finish.
workflows.interactionSequence: Set persistent guard state or surrender the remaining action budget, process contact/withdrawal reactions, and advance initiative.
workflows.committedOutcome: Guard state and actor advancement persist through later movement and save boundaries.

workflows.name: Retreat or escape
workflows.trigger: A player chooses Escape, reaches the edge band, or a routed monster flees.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate explicit escape gates or edge behavior, resolve withdrawal attacks, confirm when required, remove the actor, apply prestige, and continue battle.
workflows.committedOutcome: Only the escaping actor leaves; penalties, positions, reactions, and outcome checks persist.

workflows.name: Resolve victory, defeat, or battle return
workflows.trigger: Battle outcome becomes terminal after actions and pending macros.
workflows.interactionSequence: Drain death macros, retain or remove footprints, determine victory/defeat/escape, stage rewards or party loss, then resume the originating scenario or exploration.
workflows.committedOutcome: Outcome, surviving actors, macros, rewards transition, VM continuation, and return location commit once.

gaps.summary: Ordinary victory and reward return work, but the terminal combat workflow is not yet accepted.
gaps.evidence: An ordinary AOGM battle completed through victory, no-allies handling, exact-item treasure, Pool and Share, experience award, combat cleanup, return to exploration, and post-battle save. A synthetic MCP capture now keeps Attack, Defend, Finish, Escape, and eight movement choices reachable at 960 by 600 without covering the tactical board. Defeat, retreat, an actual level-up, user acceptance, and ordinary target-selection evidence remain gaps.
gaps.nextAction: Obtain ordinary-play acceptance of the corrected command deck, then exercise ordinary defeat or retreat and a reward that produces a level-up.

gaps.summary: Battle reward modes 5 and 10 and opcode 48 bonus treasure remain unresolved end to end.
gaps.evidence: Providence schema v2 already preserves all five positional EDCD words. Castle mode 5 still consumes monster-money RNG and can grant incidental items despite its experience-only comment; mode 10 restores equipment/wealth and separately bypasses Party Death to restart an encounter; opcode 48 opens a second fixed-treasure workspace.
gaps.nextAction: Characterize the suspicious mode-5 incidental/RNG branches and mode-10 restart field with controlled Castle fixtures, then implement each distinct runtime continuation without changing schema v2 unless the fixture disproves positional preservation.

workflows.name: Distribute treasure
workflows.trigger: Opcode 10 or 65, battle victory, or another authored reward grants treasure.
workflows.interactionSequence: Display money and items, let the player assign or reject eligible items, enforce capacities, complete distribution, and return to the issuing flow.
workflows.committedOutcome: Money, exact item instances, remaining treasure, continuation, and RNG persist through every choice.

gaps.summary: Castle's two incidental random-item draws and battle-mode interaction are not yet reproduced.
gaps.evidence: The source performs two less-than-ten checks for parchment 806 and ration 877, including after XP-only mode clears ordinary loot; whether certified scenarios depend on this is unresolved.
gaps.nextAction: Use controlled Castle RNG fixtures for ordinary, XP-only, and bonus-treasure battle rewards before implementing or correcting the random drops.

workflows.name: Detect and identify treasure
workflows.trigger: The treasure workspace offers detection or identification before distribution.
workflows.interactionSequence: Choose detection/identification, resolve source chances and costs, reveal permitted item information, and continue with the same treasure pool.
workflows.committedOutcome: Knowledge state, any cost, RNG, and remaining treasure persist.

workflows.name: Recover fumbled battle items
workflows.trigger: Battle ends with exact player items in the dropped-item queue.
workflows.interactionSequence: After body-count selection, choose recipients for each recoverable item or leave it, honoring capacity and exact instance state.
workflows.committedOutcome: Recovered instances retain charges and state; unrecovered items leave the session; continuation persists.

workflows.name: Select post-battle allies and body count
workflows.trigger: Battle cleanup offers surviving allies or source body-count choices.
workflows.interactionSequence: Present eligible allies in source order, choose permitted survivors, commit roster changes, then continue reward processing.
workflows.committedOutcome: Ally selection and battle cleanup remain saveable before later rewards.

workflows.name: Award experience and level up
workflows.trigger: Opcode 11, battle rewards, or accumulated experience makes a character eligible.
workflows.interactionSequence: Award source-scaled experience, detect eligible levels, present each level decision/result, apply rules in order, choose spells where required, and return.
workflows.committedOutcome: Experience, levels, attributes, conditions, abilities, spells, RNG, and continuation commit through each character boundary.

workflows.name: View an acquired map
workflows.trigger: Choose Maps or an authored display-map action after acquiring a map.
workflows.interactionSequence: List acquired map identities, select one, render its source picture and annotations, and close without simulation mutation.
workflows.committedOutcome: Only acquisition state belongs to the session; viewing is presentation-owned.

gaps.summary: Exact dungeon player-map composition is not yet proven against Castle.
gaps.evidence: The typed viewer derives a dungeon crop from authoritative topology, but Castle's centerpict and updatewalls pixel composition has not been captured in a controlled fixture.
gaps.nextAction: Capture one synthetic Castle dungeon player map and compare wall, door, secret, and party-marker pixels before declaring exact presentation parity.

gaps.summary: Classic scrolling TEXT encoding and style resources remain only partially represented.
gaps.evidence: The package preserves exact signed TEXT identity and bytes, and the viewer renders UTF-8 fixture text, but a representative legacy encoding and same-ID style resource have not been exercised end to end.
gaps.nextAction: Build a controlled scrolling-map fixture with legacy text and style resources, then define the exact decode and style conversion contract.

gaps.summary: Malformed crop starts and authored picture rectangles lack boundary observations.
gaps.evidence: Valid package geometry is deterministic, while Castle's behavior for out-of-range starts or rectangles has not been observed and is not guessed.
gaps.nextAction: Use synthetic boundary fixtures to decide whether Providence should reject, clamp, or preserve malformed geometry.

gaps.summary: Acquisition and browsing have synthetic proof but no ordinary AOGM acceptance.
gaps.evidence: Package, VM, complete-session restore, all four render modes, unavailable menu entries, exact assets, markers, and party bounds are automated; the known-reachable AOGM opcode 29 route has not been exercised through ordinary UI.
gaps.nextAction: Acquire an AOGM player map, save and reload at the immediate display boundary, then browse it from Maps/Notes through the ordinary shell.

workflows.name: Read and edit location notes
workflows.trigger: Choose Location Notes from the Maps menu.
workflows.interactionSequence: Open the notes for the current land or dungeon record stream, read records in source order, and edit or clear only the note at the party's current location.
workflows.committedOutcome: Saved player-authored notes retain map, location, source order, and darkness metadata with the playthrough; reverting an uncommitted modern draft leaves simulation unchanged.

gaps.summary: Castle's two dialog exit labels and exact cancellation semantics are not established by source alone.
gaps.evidence: Both item 1 and item 3 exit the dialog and the source writes the current record on exit. Realmz 2.0 exposes a clearly named presentation-owned Revert draft action and does not claim it reproduces either native item.
gaps.nextAction: Use a controlled Castle dialog-resource/runtime fixture to identify both labels and whether either native path can leave edited text uncommitted.

gaps.summary: Historical notes are readable in source order but do not yet recreate Castle's temporary map recentering and saved darkness view.
gaps.evidence: Typed state retains level, coordinate, record ordinal, and darkness value, while the Journal route currently renders text cards rather than a topology-backed historical-location viewport.
gaps.nextAction: Add a mutation-free note browser derived from authoritative topology and the saved darkness value, then verify land and dungeon records through MCP.

gaps.summary: Location-note creation, editing, removal, and restoration have synthetic proof only.
gaps.evidence: No ordinary campaign route has yet exercised the workflow.
gaps.nextAction: Create, revisit, edit, clear, save, and restore a location note during ordinary play once the historical-location browser is present.

workflows.name: Read the authored journal
workflows.trigger: Choose Journal after the scenario has recorded entries.
workflows.interactionSequence: Browse scenario-authored entries in source order, inspect long text, and return without gameplay mutation.
workflows.committedOutcome: Journal discovery/order remains session-owned; reading position is presentation-only.

gaps.summary: Castle's Auto Note preference and unsafe journal cursor boundary remain outside the verified authored-journal subset.
gaps.evidence: Castle persists 3,000 discovery flags but clamps journalindex2 to 5,999; Realmz 2.0 applies FD-MAPS-002 and records only IDs 0 through 2,999 through explicit Take note responses. Auto Note remains a separate preferences gap.
gaps.nextAction: Use a controlled Castle runtime fixture for empty and maximum-length Data SD2 records, then implement Auto Note only through the host preferences workflow if its complete pacing behavior is confirmed.

gaps.summary: Authored journal discovery and browsing have synthetic proof only.
gaps.evidence: Typed VM, save/restore, and presentation tests cover manual discovery and source-order rendering, but no ordinary campaign route has accepted the workspace.
gaps.nextAction: Record a positive scenario message through Take note, save/reload, and browse it through the Journal route during ordinary play.

workflows.name: Save and quick-save
workflows.trigger: Choose Save or Quick Save at a committed session boundary.
workflows.interactionSequence: Choose or reuse a slot, snapshot complete session state, write transactionally, validate readback, rotate backup, and report success/failure.
workflows.committedOutcome: A validated save envelope captures state, VM, interaction, clock, RNG, and package identity without presentation animation state.

workflows.name: Load or revert a game
workflows.trigger: Choose Load or Revert and select a valid slot.
workflows.interactionSequence: Inspect slot identity, validate the complete envelope and package hash, construct a replacement session only after success, or leave the current session untouched.
workflows.committedOutcome: A successful restore replaces the session atomically; a failure preserves current play.

workflows.name: Change Classic application preferences
workflows.trigger: Choose Preferences, speed, volume, or editable display-name options.
workflows.interactionSequence: Change presentation speed, audio volume, and source-exposed preference fields, apply immediately where safe, and persist host settings separately from gameplay.
workflows.committedOutcome: Presentation preferences persist without changing simulation rules, time, RNG, or save determinism.

gaps.summary: Classic's editable stock spell/race/caste names are not represented and may conflict with immutable package content.
gaps.evidence: Castle exposes name editors; 2.0 intentionally treats package definitions as immutable.
gaps.nextAction: Record a fidelity decision to reject, host-locally overlay, or otherwise preserve this preference without mutating packages.

gaps.summary: Classic's reduced-sound preference is not represented.
gaps.evidence: Castle persists reducesound in pref.c and suppresses modal ambience such as Swap sound 3003 while retaining action sounds; Realmz 2.0 currently exposes volume but no equivalent policy.
gaps.nextAction: Add a host-persisted reduced-sound setting and classify every source-gated modal sound before suppressing events globally.

workflows.name: Quit the application
workflows.trigger: Choose Quit or close the application window.
workflows.interactionSequence: Route menu and window-close requests through one typed host confirmation; optionally save an active noncombat session, explicitly quit without saving, or cancel; keep the process open when save fails.
workflows.committedOutcome: The process exits only after an accepted action; existing validated saves remain intact.

gaps.summary: Typed Quit choices and host transaction ordering are characterized, but the real window-close notification and save-repository failure path lack composition-root proof.
gaps.evidence: Focused tests prove save failure suppresses termination, no-save bypasses persistence, and Cancel invokes neither operation. Godot's window notification is wired to the same host request but has not been exercised through the running root.
gaps.nextAction: After package startup becomes non-blocking, inject a repository failure through RealmzApplication and exercise menu Quit plus NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST through Godot MCP Pro.

workflows.name: Discover and install packages
workflows.trigger: Open the campaign library, refresh discovery, or choose a package file.
workflows.interactionSequence: Scan approved roots, deduplicate package identity, validate an opened package, install it transactionally, and refresh the library.
workflows.committedOutcome: One validated immutable package is installed; stale/duplicate discoveries do not appear as separate campaigns.

gaps.summary: Only AOGM package installation has ordinary evidence.
gaps.evidence: Package repository tests are synthetic for other campaigns.
gaps.nextAction: Install and discover the current War export without diagnostics.

workflows.name: Explain package readiness failures
workflows.trigger: Discovery or loading rejects a package, schema, capability, reference, hash, or media requirement.
workflows.interactionSequence: Keep the package unavailable, show a specific reason and safe next action, and leave valid installed campaigns usable.
workflows.committedOutcome: No invalid content enters a session and no current session is replaced.

workflows.name: Show loading and validation progress
workflows.trigger: A large package is discovered, loaded, validated, or installed.
workflows.interactionSequence: Display non-blocking checking/progress state, preserve responsiveness, and transition to ready or exact failure.
workflows.committedOutcome: No simulation mutation occurs before validation succeeds.

workflows.name: Manage immutable character revisions
workflows.trigger: Open Vault, publish a revision, inspect history, restore, or archive.
workflows.interactionSequence: List current records, inspect revisions, publish transactionally, archive instead of delete, and recover the current index from backup when necessary.
workflows.committedOutcome: Immutable validated revisions and a recoverable current index persist outside campaign saves.

workflows.name: Import and publish campaign characters
workflows.trigger: Add an eligible vault revision to setup or explicitly publish a committed campaign character.
workflows.interactionSequence: Validate definitions/restrictions and provenance, clone into session ownership, or publish only at a safe boundary after confirmation.
workflows.committedOutcome: Campaign changes never mutate vault history silently; imports and publications retain stable provenance.

gaps.summary: Cross-campaign reuse is tested but has no ordinary AOGM-to-War evidence.
gaps.evidence: Vault import/publication tests are synthetic.
gaps.nextAction: Publish an AOGM revision and import it into a compatible second campaign.

workflows.name: Configure accessibility and presentation
workflows.trigger: Open Settings.
workflows.interactionSequence: Change text scale, audio, reduced motion, and controls; preview safely; persist host preferences; return without simulation mutation.
workflows.committedOutcome: Presentation changes persist separately and never alter rules, RNG, time, or gameplay saves.

gaps.summary: Control customization and complete multi-scale layout acceptance remain unfinished.
gaps.evidence: Settings persist, but controls are deferred and target resolution/text-scale acceptance is incomplete.
gaps.nextAction: Finish keyboard/mouse control help and run layout acceptance at every locked resolution and text scale.

workflows.name: Browse save previews and package identity
workflows.trigger: Open Save or Load from System.
workflows.interactionSequence: List slots with campaign/package identity, metadata and validity, distinguish mismatches/corruption, then select a safe operation.
workflows.committedOutcome: Browsing is read-only; load replaces the session only after full validation.

workflows.name: Certify release builds
workflows.trigger: Prepare a Windows, macOS, or Linux release candidate.
workflows.interactionSequence: Export without gallery/MCP/commercial data, install the same Safe package, run required workflows, save/reload, and verify clean rejection surfaces.
workflows.committedOutcome: A reproducible release artifact behaves identically on every supported platform.

gaps.summary: There is no cross-platform release certification and no accepted release candidate.
gaps.evidence: Development and local Windows runs do not satisfy the locked release gate.
gaps.nextAction: After Classic blockers close, produce clean exports and run the same Safe package on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
